paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Israel moves when God moves. The cloud lifted, and the whole nation set out "according to the LORD’s command through Moses" (Numbers 10:13). They didn't leave because they got restless or because somebody drew up a great plan. Following God means we go when He says go and stay when He says stay, and that's a lot easier on the nerves than guessing.

Notice the other thing in this passage. Moses hears a flat "No" from Hobab and comes right back with "Please do not leave us" (Numbers 10:31). I think Moses knew something I need to hear: God's people are better together, and a good invitation is worth asking twice. Moses also promised, "we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us" (Numbers 10:32). So who in your life needs a second invitation from YOU?

And look at what Moses says when the ark moves. Whenever the ark set out, he would say, "Rise up, O LORD!" (Numbers 10:35), and when it came to rest, he would say, "Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel." (Numbers 10:36). Every time the ark moved or stopped, Moses turned to the LORD. So go ahead and make your own plans, baker, but bring Him into your starts and your stops too.
